s1.syndrome_frame: Palpitations and syncope in a patient with complex congenital heart disease
salient_findings: Tachycardia with heart rate of 183 bpm
Irregularly irregular tachycardia with grouped beating on ECG
key_facts: Patient has complex congenital heart disease
Patient has D-transposition of the great arteries
Patient has single ventricle physiology
Patient has Fontan circulation
Patient experiences lightheadedness and syncope with walking
Patient has persistent tachycardia and palpitations
ECG shows irregularly irregular tachycardia with grouped beating
Transesophageal echocardiogram shows no intracardiac thrombus
Patient is prescribed diltiazem and apixaban
Heart rate is 183 bpm in the emergency department

raw.syndrome_frame: Palpitations and syncope in a patient with complex congenital heart disease
salient_findings: Tachycardia with heart rate of 183 bpm
Irregularly irregular tachycardia with grouped beating on ECG

raw.rationale: The ECG shows irregularly irregular tachycardia with grouped beating and intermittently visible P waves, which is consistent with atrial fibrillation, especially given the patient's complex congenital heart disease and Fontan circulation.

rejected.label: Atrial flutter
rejected.why: Atrial flutter typically presents with a regular rhythm, which is not seen in this patient's initial ECG.

rejected.label: Orthodromic atrioventricular reentrant tachycardia
rejected.why: This condition usually presents with a regular, narrow complex tachycardia, which is not consistent with the initial irregularly irregular rhythm seen in this patient.

rejected.label: Focal atrial tachycardia
rejected.why: Focal atrial tachycardia typically presents with a regular rhythm and P waves that are different from the patient's native P waves, which is not seen in this case.

rejected.label: Atrioventricular nodal reentrant tachycardia
rejected.why: This condition usually presents with a regular, narrow complex tachycardia and is not consistent with the irregularly irregular rhythm seen in this patient's initial ECG.
